sentences: The f16 of every d16 result (image samples and gathers, the `image_sample_c_lz` compare result, typed buffer loads) and of the f16 formats a typed buffer store writes is narrowed with integer ops (`Gen.f16_bits`; #489, #711), not with `PackHalf2x16`: to nearest even, except the typed-buffer float conversions, which round toward zero (below).

AMD drivers lower `PackHalf2x16` to `v_cvt_pkrtz_f16_f32`, which rounds toward zero (#489), and there about half of all unorm8, unorm16 and snorm8 values loaded with d16 came out 1 ulp low (123 of 256, 31,742 of 65,536 and 110 of 256).
Packed MUBUF and MTBUF loads clamp unsigned 32-bit channels to 65535 before writing each half.
On native gfx1036, values 65534 and 65535 survived, while 65536, 65537 and 0xffffffff all produced 0xffff, across all four load widths in wave32 and wave64.
Packed `buffer_load_format_d16_x` and `_xyz` write only the low 16 bits of the final VGPR.
Its upper half survives even when the load is out of bounds.
Native gfx1036 wave32 and wave64 confirmed this with RGBA8_UINT and RGBA8_UNORM, two destination seeds, and both even-component loads as full-write controls.
Full pairs are packed by `pack_f16_pair_int` and an odd final buffer component is narrowed with `f16_bits` for float/normalized formats.
These memory conversions do not use `f16_pack2`: they come from the texture and buffer units, not the VALU whose rounding `MODE.FP_ROUND` sets (#753).

**Typed buffer floats are narrowed toward zero (SHADER-358).** Measured natively on gfx1036 (RDNA2, wave32 and wave64, `tools/hw_oracle`): `buffer_store_format_*` into `16_FLOAT`/`16_16_FLOAT`/`16_16_16_16_FLOAT` and `buffer_load_format_d16_*` from `32_FLOAT`/`32_32_FLOAT`/`32_32_32_32_FLOAT` round an f32 toward zero, give ±65504 for a finite value past the f16 range (65520 stores 0x7bff, not infinity), flush an f32 denormal to a signed zero, keep infinities, and keep a NaN's sign and top 10 payload bits without quieting it (1 if those are 0: 0x7fa00000 gives 0x7d00, 0x7f800001 gives 0x7c01); gfx1150 does the same for the stores (#1548).
The translator does that with `Gen.mem_f16`; until 2026-11-22 it rounded these to nearest even and overflowed to infinity.
UNORM/SNORM d16 loads keep the rounding above (nearest even of the exact quotient, re-measured on gfx1036 for every 8-bit value and a 16-bit sample).
Checked by `tests/semantic/test_buffer_f16_narrowing_hw.py` (45 measured values in four forms).

Image d16 results are still inferred to round to nearest even (SHADER-308). #489's own narrower, `f32_to_f16_int`, was folded into `f16_bits` on 2026-11-22: the two gave the same bits on 30,648 inputs (every f32 exponent, ties, the subnormal and overflow edges, NaN), and `f16_bits` lost its one GLSL.std.450 instruction (`UMin`) so the packer stays free of them.
For typed buffer loads the rounding is measured (BUILD-161, `tools/d16_format_probe.py`).

On an RX 6700 (gfx1031, AMD Windows driver 32.0.21045.29003), every UNORM8, SNORM8, UNORM10, UNORM16 and SNORM16 value was loaded through `buffer_load_format_d16_x` and `tbuffer_load_format_d16_x`, in wave32 and wave64.
The hardware rounds the exact quotient once, straight to f16, to nearest even, with f16 denormals kept (65,536 of 65,536 UNORM16 and SNORM16 values).
It does not round to f32 first: that double rounding is 1 ulp high on exactly four values (UNORM16 0xffaf and 0xffef, SNORM16 0x7ff7 and 0x8009).
Over every width from 1 to 16 bits, only two f32 quotients land on an f16 halfway point: 0x3f7ff000 (16379/16383, 32759/32767, 65519/65535) and 0x3f7fb000 (65455/65535).
`Gen.d16_norm_f16` takes the f16 below for those two, for normalized formats only; a 32_FLOAT 0x3f7ff000 is a real tie and still rounds to even.
`buffer_load_format_x` without d16 returned the correctly rounded f32 quotient for all of them, the decode `norm_bits` builds.
A 16_FLOAT d16 load returned its own bits for all 65,536 encodings.
MUBUF and MTBUF agreed everywhere.

For d16 image results, round to nearest even is still inferred, as in #489, not measured. #489's own narrower, `f32_to_f16_int`, was folded into `f16_bits` on 2026-11-22: the two gave the same bits on 30,648 inputs (every f32 exponent, ties, the subnormal and overflow edges, NaN), and `f16_bits` lost its one GLSL.std.450 instruction (`UMin`) so the packer stays free of them.

Checked by `tests/test_translate.py` (`test_depth_compare_sample_result_width`, `test_buffer_format_f16_narrowing_avoids_packhalf2x16`), `tests/test_d16_pack.py` and `tests/semantic/test_buffer_load_format.py` (`D16NormalizedRounding`).
